problem: 'Knock is uncontrolled detonation after the spark' is loose. Standard texts define knock as autoignition of the end gas ahead of the flame front, which gives the sharp pressure rise; 'detonation' is a related but distinct term and some examiners mark this as a misuse.
fix: Knock is the autoignition of the unburnt end gas ahead of the flame front after the spark. It burns very fast and gives a sharp pressure rise that hits the block at the knock frequency.

problem: The knock window is said to open 'around top dead centre'. Knock normally appears after the spark, roughly 10–40° after TDC in the combustion period, so 'around TDC' can make a student expect a symmetric window on both sides of TDC.
fix: The ECU opens a crank-angle window just after top dead centre, over the combustion period, and compares the envelope with a threshold inside that window.

problem: A rectifier on its own does not produce an envelope; the envelope comes only when the rectified signal is smoothed by a low-pass filter. The block diagram shows 'Rectifier → envelope' with no smoothing element.
fix: A rectifier followed by a low-pass filter makes the envelope of the knock signal. Label the block 'Rectifier + low-pass filter (envelope)'.

problem: LIDAR and flex-fuel composition sensing sit outside the chapter title (knock, acceleration and torque sensors). The chapter itself points to Unit 5 for detail, so carrying a full LIDAR formula, a worked quiz question and exam traps on it risks duplication and confusion about which unit to revise.
fix: Keep a one-line mention that LIDAR time of flight (d = c t / 2) and flex-fuel dielectric sensing belong to the ADAS and fuel-system units, and move the LIDAR calculation and its trap to that unit.
